title: Review 3: Notation, yarn diameter and textured weaves

quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: Terms from number systems, yarn geometry and textured weaves.

questions.q: In hexadecimal weave notation, one hexadecimal number describes
questions.explain: Each pick is a row of lifted (1) and lowered (0) ends, written as a hex number; the weave is a list of them from the bottom pick upward.

questions.q: A nibble is
questions.explain: Four bits make one hexadecimal digit, 0 to F.

questions.q: In the weave notation, a binary 1 means
questions.explain: 1 = end lifted (a filled square on point paper); 0 = end down.

questions.q: Specific volume of a yarn is
options: The space taken by one gram of it
questions.explain: About 1.1 cm³ per gram for cotton yarn in cloth; it links count to diameter.

questions.q: A crepe weave is recognised by
options: An all-over, pebbly surface with no clear lines
questions.explain: The interlacings are scattered irregularly, usually built on a sateen base.

questions.q: A honeycomb weave is used for towels because
options: Its ridges of long floats and hollow cells take up water well
questions.explain: The cellular surface gives a large, absorbent area.

questions.q: In a Bedford cord, the cutting ends
options: Weave plain with every pick and make the sunk line between cords
questions.explain: They bind firmly on every pick, so the cloth sinks between the raised cords.

questions.q: Stuffer (wadding) ends in a Bedford cord lie almost straight inside the cord to make it fuller.
questions.explain: They are lifted on the floating picks and lowered on the weaving picks, so they stay between face and back.

questions.q: The cords of a Bedford cord run
questions.explain: Bedford cord has warp-way ribs; piqué (welt) cords run weft-way.

questions.q: The hexadecimal digit F stands for four lifted ends in a row.
questions.explain: F = 1111 in binary, so all four ends of that group are up.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: How the notation, the yarn and the structure follow from simple rules.

questions.q: Why is a weave written in hexadecimal instead of binary?
options: Hex is shorter: one digit replaces four bits
questions.explain: The information is identical; hexadecimal just packs four ends into one character.

questions.q: A design is 6 ends wide. Before grouping each pick into hex digits, you
options: Add two idle zero ends on the right to make 8
Add two ones on the left
questions.explain: Zeros are added on the right to fill the last nibble and are dropped again when decoding; “−6” records the true width.

questions.q: As a yarn gets coarser (higher tex), its diameter
options: Rises in proportion to the square root of the tex
Rises in proportion to the tex
questions.explain: d = √tex ÷ 26.7 mm: four times the tex gives twice the diameter.

questions.q: Yarn A is Ne 9 and yarn B is Ne 36. The diameter of A is
questions.explain: d is proportional to 1 ÷ √Ne: 1/3 against 1/6, so A is twice as thick.

questions.q: A crepe weave is commonly built by
options: Adding marks to the points of a sateen base
questions.explain: The scattered sateen points, each given the same small addition, produce an irregular all-over texture.

questions.q: A honeycomb is produced by combining
options: A straight draft with a twill peg plan
A pointed draft with a pointed lifting plan
A satin draft with plain lifting
questions.explain: Reversal in both directions makes the diamond-shaped cells.

questions.q: In a Bedford cord, the weft floats on the back of a cord
options: Pull the cord up into a rounded ridge
questions.explain: The loose floats contract and the plain-woven face above them bulges.

questions.q: The hex code $9 $C $6 $3 −4 is a 2/2 twill.
questions.explain: 1001, 1100, 0110, 0011: two up and two down on every pick, stepping one end each pick.

questions.q: Yarn diameter matters to a designer mainly because it decides
options: How closely threads can be set and how much of the cloth they cover
questions.explain: Cover and the maximum sett both follow from diameter compared with spacing.

questions.q: A number written with zeros added on the left has a changed value.
questions.explain: 0110 1101 is still 109. In the weave notation the padding zeros go on the right of each pick only because they stand for idle ends.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Conversions and diameters to work out.

questions.q: Convert binary 1011 to decimal.
Convert hexadecimal $1F to decimal.
Convert binary 1101101 to decimal.
How many ends are lifted on a pick coded $A5 in an 8-end design?
questions.explain: $A5 = 1010 0101, which has 4 ones.

questions.q: How many hexadecimal digits are needed for each pick of a 12-end design?
questions.explain: 12 ends ÷ 4 = 3 digits.

questions.q: How many hexadecimal digits are needed for each pick of a 10-end design?
questions.explain: 10 ends are padded to 12 with two zeros, giving 3 digits.

questions.q: What is the diameter in mm of a Ne 36 cotton yarn, using d = 0.9 ÷ √Ne? Answer to two decimals.
What is the diameter in mm of a 64 tex yarn, using d = √tex ÷ 26.7? Answer to two decimals.
Using d = 1 ÷ (28 √Ne) inches, how many Ne 25 threads laid side by side and touching fill one inch?
questions.explain: Threads per inch = 28 × √25 = 140.

questions.q: A plain-face Bedford cord repeat has two cords, each of 10 face ends, with 2 cutting ends beside each cord. How many ends are in the repeat?

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: A honeycomb towel from draft to dobby code.

questions.q: How many heald frames does the design need?
questions.explain: The highest number in the draft 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 is 5.

questions.q: How many hexadecimal digits are needed for each pick?
questions.explain: 8 ends ÷ 4 = 2 digits per pick.

questions.q: A pick on which only ends 1 and 5 are lifted is written
questions.explain: Ends 1 and 5 are the leftmost bit of each nibble: 1000 1000 = $88.

questions.q: How many of the 8 ends are lifted on a pick coded $7C?
questions.explain: $7C = 0111 1100, which has 5 ones.

questions.q: Which ends are lifted on a pick coded $44?
questions.explain: $44 = 0100 0100: the second bit of each nibble, so ends 2 and 6.

questions.q: What is the diameter of the yarn in mm, using d = 0.9 ÷ √Ne? Answer to three decimals.
What is the count of the yarn in tex, to one decimal? Use tex = 590.5 ÷ Ne.
Ends 2 and 8 are drawn on the same heald. This means that
options: They move identically on every pick
They pass through the same dent
One of them is a stuffer end
questions.explain: Ends on one heald rise and fall together; that is what a pointed draft uses to save frames.

questions.q: The buyer asks for a larger cell: the same honeycomb on 16 ends, drafted 1 to 9 and back to 2. How many heald frames does that need?
questions.explain: The pointed draft 1 2 … 9 … 3 2 uses 9 frames for 16 ends.

questions.q: Because the draft is pointed, ends 4 and 6 of the repeat are on the same heald.
questions.explain: The draft reads 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2: the fourth and sixth ends are both on heald 4.

quizzes.case: A towel is designed as an ordinary 8-end honeycomb. It is drafted 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 (a pointed draft) and its lifting plan is also pointed, on 8 picks. Warp and weft are Ne 16 cotton. The design is sent to an electronic dobby as one hexadecimal code per pick, with the first end as the leftmost bit.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Decoding, designing and reasoning across the four lectures.

questions.q: Decode $8 $4 $2 −3. The weave is
questions.explain: Dropping the padding zero: 100, 010, 001. One end up, two down, stepping one end each pick: a 1/2 twill.

questions.q: Which hex code is plain weave on 4 ends?
questions.explain: $A = 1010 and $5 = 0101: alternate ends up, reversing on the next pick.

questions.q: Convert decimal 200 to hexadecimal and enter the value of its first (left) digit as a decimal number.
questions.explain: 200 = 12 × 16 + 8 = $C8; the first digit C is 12.

questions.q: Two yarns are 16 tex and 64 tex. How many times thicker is the second, using d = √tex ÷ 26.7?
A yarn has a diameter of 0.20 mm. How many such threads, touching side by side, fit in 100 mm?
A 4/1 satin on five ends is written in the hexadecimal notation. On each pick, the number of 1 bits among the five ends is
questions.explain: Satin is warp-faced: four of the five ends are up on every pick.

questions.q: A designer wants a cord cloth with ribs running along the warp and a plain face. The structure to choose is
questions.explain: Bedford cord gives warp-way cords with a plain or twill face.

questions.q: A crepe built on an 8-end sateen base normally has a repeat of 8 ends and 8 picks.
questions.explain: The added marks follow the base points, so the repeat stays that of the base.

questions.q: In a Bedford cord woven with red picks for one cord’s face and green picks for the other, each cord shows
options: A mixture of red and green
One solid colour, because only its own weaving picks are on its face
questions.explain: The other colour floats on the back of that cord, hidden from the face.

questions.q: An 8-end pick has ends 1, 2, 7 and 8 lifted. Write it in hex and enter the decimal value of the two-digit hex number.
